To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the uncertainty relations applicable to the time and energy differences of quark pairs are identical to the relationships between the widths and the lifetimes of unstable hadrons and, therefore, the uncertainty relations applicable for the space and time separa­tions of the quark pairs are the same as the relationships between the space and time widths of hadrons, and that these relationships are covariant.

(1) the time-energy uncertainty principle can be combined with the position-momentum uncertainty principle to give the uncertainty relation in a covariant and Lorentz-invariant form; (2) this effect manifests itself through Feynman's parton picture; and (3) the time-energy and position-momentum uncertainty principles are equivalent to each other.

the time‐time and time‐energy uncertainty relations can be combined with the position‐momentum and momentum‐momentum uncertainty relations to give a covariant uncertainty principle, and that the effect manifests itself in the parton picture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the uncertainty relations applicable to the quarks in the hadron.
the uncertainty relation in space‐time separations between quarks in hadrons.
the uncertainty relations for space and time separable variables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, if the uncertainty relation between time and energy is to be taken seriously, then the uncertainty relation between space and energy should also be taken seriously.
, if the uncertainty relation in the space‐time separations between the partons in a hadron is to be maintained, then the uncertainty relation in energy and time separations should also be satisfied.

the time‐space separation uncertainty relations are Lorentz covariant and that the Lorentz covariance of the time‐energy separation relation is a direct consequence of the Lorentz invariance of the energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the uncertainty relations in the space‐time separations between the constituents of a hadron are Lorentz covariant.

the time‐like and space‐like uncertainty relations can be combined to give the uncertainty relations applicable to the space‐time separation between the quarks and that these are Lorentz covariant relations.
the time‐like parton picture can be derived from the space‐like parton model by the time‐energy relation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uncertainty principle in space‐time is the same as that between the width and lifetime of an unstable particle.
the time‐uncertainty relation between the time of a hadron and the time of a parton is the same as Heisenberg’s uncertainty relation.
the time‐uncertainty relation is a direct consequence of Lorentz covariance, which in turn is a direct consequence from the fact that the speed of light is the maximum velocity in the universe.
